methods.label: Separate one-digit and two-digit hours
methods.explanation:
Using the display format in the examples, the hours \(1\) through \(9\) have one digit, while the minutes always have two digits. Count these separately from hours \(10\), \(11\), and \(12\).

For a one-digit hour \(h\), the three displayed digits form a palindrome exactly when the minute's ones digit is also \(h\). Its tens digit can be any of \(0,1,2,3,4,5\), since minutes run from \(00\) through \(59\). Thus each of the nine one-digit hours contributes six palindromes, for \(9\cdot6=54\).

For a two-digit hour, the two minute digits must be the hour digits in reverse order. This gives exactly
\[
10{:}01,\qquad 11{:}11,\qquad 12{:}21.
\]
All three are valid times. Every hour occurs once in a twelve-hour cycle, the two cases cover all hours, and each permitted minute is counted once. Therefore the total is
\[
54+3=\boxed{57},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
